The scan confirms the duplication, and reading the files backs it up. `sanitizeUserInput` (`src/sanitize-a.ts:10-36`), `sanitizeText` (`src/sanitize-b.ts:9-35`) and `cleanMessage` (`src/sanitize-c.ts:9-35`) are the same function under different names. Finding `crime_00002` gives all three the same body hash, `289f7da71f3a`. Only the parameter and local variable names differ (`raw`/`working`, `input`/`cleaned`, `value`/`normalised`). The limits, regexes and thresholds are identical in all three, so there's nothing that needs to become a parameter.

## Proposed public API

A new file, `src/sanitize.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Normalise free-text user input. Returns "" for null/empty input and for input
 * that looks hostile (leading angle bracket, "\x" escapes, heavy !?! runs).
 * Truncates to 1000 chars; lowercases shouty (>90% caps, >30 chars) text.
 */
export function sanitizeText(raw: string): string;
```

- **One function, one string argument, no options object.** The three copies don't vary in anything, so a `{ maxLength, lowercaseShouting, … }` config would add settings nobody uses. Add a parameter later only when a caller actually needs different behaviour.
- **Name:** `sanitizeText`, because it describes what the function does. It's already the export in `sanitize-b.ts`, so one of the three call paths keeps its name.
- **Move the body over exactly as it is.** In particular, keep the character-class regex on line 13 (`/[ -]/g`) byte-for-byte. It probably contains control characters that don't display, so copy it rather than retyping it.

## Files that would change

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/sanitize.ts` (new) | Holds the single `sanitizeText` implementation. |
| `src/sanitize-a.ts` | Delete the body. Keep `export { sanitizeText as sanitizeUserInput } from "./sanitize"` only if something outside this repo imports it. |
| `src/sanitize-b.ts` | Delete the body. Re-export `sanitizeText` from `./sanitize`, or delete the file. |
| `src/sanitize-c.ts` | Delete the body. Keep `export { sanitizeText as cleanMessage }` as a deprecated alias, or delete it. |

The scan shows 0 direct and 0 transitive importers for these files (`blast_radius: 0`). So the simplest version deletes all three wrappers and leaves `src/sanitize.ts` as the only module. Keep the aliases only if these files are a public package surface. There are no tests in the fixture, so before deleting anything, add a small test of `sanitizeText`: null input, the 1000-char cutoff, a leading `<`, a `\x` escape, the `!?!` threshold and the caps-lowering case.

## Keep these out of this refactor

- **The admin guards in `sanitize-*.ts` behave differently, so they can't be merged as-is.** This is `crime_00001`. `assertAdminA` checks `role === "admin"`. `assertAdminB` checks `role === "admin" || role === "owner"`. `assertAdminC` checks `role !== "admin"`, so it returns **true for non-admins**, which is either inverted or misnamed. Moving them into one `isAdmin(role)` would quietly change how B and C behave. Decide the intended rule first. After that, `src/policy.ts` can share one helper: `canEditBilling`, `canSeeAuditLog` and `canImpersonate` really are identical. Because of this, I'd also leave the guards in place while gutting the sanitize files: they're a separate change with different risks.
- **The telemetry files are a separate, easy fix.** This is `crime_00003`. `recordSanitiseEvent` is exactly the same in `telemetry-a.ts` and `telemetry-b.ts`, so it can move into one module. That's also the natural moment to pass in a clock (`now: () => number = Date.now`), which clears `crime_00004` and `crime_00005`.
